director.chapterArc: A tactical breakthrough regarding power mechanics (non-contact hold) followed by a strategic debate where Callie rejects Katori's plan for personal agency, culminating in an emotional confrontation with her mother about autonomy and sacrifice before the ascent begins.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Calm. The scene is defined by arithmetic precision and quiet resolve rather than dramatic outbursts. Character voices must remain distinct but grounded; do not let Katori's flat authority or Callie's analytical internal monologue drift into melodrama. The mother's declaration of agency should feel like a factual correction, not a plea.

cues.delivery: Otto's observation is dry and observational; he speaks to the mechanics of failure without self-pity.
cues.from: It was Otto's idea, and he had it by accident. He was sitting on the bank on the west side of the lay-by with his sling across his chest, watching her try for the fourth time. He watched the pale go into the conduit and flicker at the bottom and drain back out of it, the pipe first and the hook after. And he said, not to anybody, "It always goes out of the pipe first."
cues.through: "The pipe's not yours," said Otto. He went red. "I mean — it's not hers. Your grandfather's. The hook was his for sixty years. The pipe came out of a wall."

cues.delivery: Callie's internal process is rhythmic and precise; treat the counting as a metronome of physical sensation.
cues.from: There was a boulder in the bank at the side of the lay-by, grey stone the size of a cart, with a crack running down its face. Callie put the point of the hook into the crack and seated it, and put her hand flat on the back of the curve. She dropped her weight and set her back foot and braced, through the steel, the way her mother had told her. She did not grip it. She let the steel be the place she planted.
cues.through: The fourth time something happened that she did not understand.

cues.delivery: The realization is delivered with flat surprise; the narrator must not dramatize the 'magic' but treat it as a physical anomaly.
cues.from: She had seated the hook and braced through it, and the pale was in the steel and steady. At about twenty, Otto called something from the wagon. It was a question about the harness, whether the breeching strap would take a horse pulling the wrong way. Callie turned her head to answer him. Without thinking, the way you let go of a thing to point, she took her hand off the hook.
cues.through: "No," said Katori. "Neither do I. Remember it anyway."
cues.reason: Shift from action to conceptual discovery.

cues.delivery: Pell's planning is dry and logistical; his tone should be matter-of-fact even when discussing danger.
cues.from: They planned the hill at supper. It was the longest supper Callie had ever sat through.
cues.through: Nobody laughed. Callie wasn't sure he had meant anybody to.

cues.delivery: Callie's rejection is logical and firm; she speaks facts about the physics of the situation without emotional pleading.
cues.through: "And it's three days lit," said Callie. "Three days of it coming out of me. I held it thirteen hours on the causeway and it took me two days to get a hand of water back in the well. I'd be empty by noon on the first day. I'd be a girl standing in a road with nothing, in front of everything on the high plain." She put the stick down. "I'll be lit as long as the wagon's on the pitch. A minute and a half. Not one second longer. Then I go dark, and nothing on the plain can feel me, and nothing comes."

cues.delivery: Katori's acceptance is flat and relieved; Ines's brief interaction carries a dry, functional warmth.
cues.from: Katori looked at her for a long time across the fire.
cues.through: "After," Ines agreed. It was the nearest thing to a smile Callie had seen on her.

cues.delivery: The mother's speech is measured and authoritative; she speaks with a quiet finality that overrides the group's concern.
cues.from: Otto wanted the horse. He said so all at once, as if he had been holding it in his mouth all through supper. "I'll be on the top with her. On the fall. She knows me. She'll go for me. She — " He stopped and looked at Callie. "She'll go for me if you're not near her. You'll be down at the hook. That's twenty paces at least, and past the lip, where she can't see you. She'll go."
cues.through: "There," said her mother, and looked away, and pulled the blanket up. "That's settled. Somebody put more wood on this fire. I'm cold."
cues.reason: Character moment of high emotional weight delivered without melodrama.

cues.delivery: The night scene is intimate and quiet; the narrator should drop volume slightly to convey the stillness of the moment.
cues.from: Her mother went off in the night, a little after two.
cues.through: Callie did not go to sleep. But she lay down, and let her wrist be held, and after a while that was nearly the same.

cues.delivery: The morning sequence is functional and observational; the mother's transformation should feel subtle and physical.
cues.from: She went back down and told them, and they went.
cues.through: Then she turned round, and went to put her shoulder to the back of a wagon.

cues.delivery: The final ascent is tense but controlled; the narrator must maintain a steady rhythm as the physical effort begins.
cues.from: The lower part of the steep took them two hours.
cues.through: "Pull," Callie said. She said it not very loud, because the air was still, and on the top of the scarp Otto heard her and said it again to the horse. "Pull."

He watched the pale go into the conduit and flicker at the bottom and drain back out of it, the pipe first and the hook after. And he said, not to anybody, "It always goes out of the pipe first."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Otto's observation; allows listener to register the mechanic of failure.
Emphasis on the critical mechanic that drives the breakthrough.

pauses.after: Callie sat down on the gravel. Half the well was gone. It was the same half-well as before, but it had bought twice as much.
pauses.reason: Major realization: The hook holds longer without contact. A moment for the concept to land before moving on.

pauses.reason: Isolating the value of the discovery for emphasis.

pauses.after: She looked at it. She looked at it hard, the way you look at a thing you're afraid is going to fall. And as she looked at it, the pale began to go thin at the point. She stepped forward and got her hand back on it, fast, and it held for another four or five seconds, and went out.
pauses.reason: Scene turn from action back to dialogue; reset after the physical demonstration of the new mechanic.

Emphasizing Katori's validation and the shift in authority.

pauses.after: "It's mine to spend," said her mother. "You said it yourself, today, to Pell, about your tenth. It's mine. I'm saying it now." She held Callie's eyes. "You don't get to spend me, love. Not even on keeping me."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Callie's mother asserts her agency. A pause to let the weight of 'You don't get to spend me' settle.

pauses.before: You don't get to spend me,
pauses.reason: Critical line of agency; isolating 'me' for emotional weight.

pauses.after: "I'm still walking up that hill," said her mother.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; transition from the mother's internal state back to dialogue with Callie.

pauses.before: I've been dying for three months,
pauses.reason: Emphasizing the mother's casual acceptance of her mortality.

pauses.after: "Oh," she said, in a slightly different voice. "Oh, yes. I see."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the ash taking effect. A breath before she gives her instruction.

pauses.after: Then she turned round, and went to put her shoulder to the back of a wagon.
